# The Software Factory Manifesto

> Best practices for a fully automated software factory where AI agents turn requests into merged, verified changes. Three levels: README (overview), docs/NN-theme/README.md (theme), docs/NN-theme/*.md (subtopic). All rules by id: RULES.md. How to use: AGENTS.md.

## Start

- [README.md](README.md): thesis, nine principles, factory map, reading paths
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): how agents should read, apply and cite this manifesto
- [RULES.md](RULES.md): every rule by id with links

## 00-journey

- [docs/00-journey/README.md](docs/00-journey/README.md): Follow one real request, a bug reported in chat, through the nine stages of the factory, seeing who acts, what goes in and out, and how the job state changes at each step.
- [docs/00-journey/01-request-arrives.md](docs/00-journey/01-request-arrives.md): Stage 1. Ana's chat message is verified by the intake service and becomes issue 412, linked to her thread; she gets a link back in seconds.
- [docs/00-journey/02-triage.md](docs/00-journey/02-triage.md): Stage 2. A read-only triage agent reads the request, the spec and the code, and returns a verdict (kind bug, risk low, size S, criteria, plan); a script applies it to the issue.
- [docs/00-journey/03-dispatch.md](docs/00-journey/03-dispatch.md): Stage 3. A deterministic dispatcher starts exactly one build run for issue 412, guarded against duplicate events, and the job script moves the job to building.
- [docs/00-journey/04-build.md](docs/00-journey/04-build.md): Stage 4. The builder agent works in a disposable sandbox; because the kind is bug, it first writes a test that fails on main, then fixes the code until the test passes.
- [docs/00-journey/05-gate.md](docs/00-journey/05-gate.md): Stage 5. One gate script (lint, format, types, tests, build, repository rules) must pass before any pull request exists; the same script runs in hooks and in CI.
- [docs/00-journey/06-pull-request.md](docs/00-journey/06-pull-request.md): Stage 6. The builder opens a pull request whose description proves the fix (test output before and after, a screenshot) criterion by criterion; scripts label it and the job moves to reviewing.
- [docs/00-journey/07-review.md](docs/00-journey/07-review.md): Stage 7. A separate reviewer agent with a clean context checks the PR against the criteria and the evidence; it asks for one change, the builder fixes it, and the second round is approved.
- [docs/00-journey/08-merge.md](docs/00-journey/08-merge.md): Stage 8. A merge script checks a fixed list of conditions (risk, kind, protected paths, review, hold, CI); Ana's low-risk bug passes all of them and is merged without a person.
- [docs/00-journey/09-notify-and-learn.md](docs/00-journey/09-notify-and-learn.md): Stage 9. Ana gets the merge notice in her thread, the job records cost and time, each agent saves what it learned, and a repeated correction becomes a new lint rule.
- [docs/00-journey/feature.md](docs/00-journey/feature.md): The same journey for a feature, "add a date filter to the CSV export"; triage asks a question first, the builder maps each criterion to a test, and a person always approves.
- [docs/00-journey/incident.md](docs/00-journey/incident.md): The same journey for an incident that starts from an alert; the factory races to a candidate fix with a regression test, and the on-call person decides whether to merge.

## 01-work-intake

- [docs/01-work-intake/README.md](docs/01-work-intake/README.md): Take work where people already ask for it, let a read-only triage step set its risk, kind and size, and send only small, clear, opted-in jobs to a builder.
- [docs/01-work-intake/intake-surfaces.md](docs/01-work-intake/intake-surfaces.md): Accept work from chat, issues and alerts, turn each request into the same kind of tracked item linked to where it came from, and report back on that same thread.
- [docs/01-work-intake/request-kinds.md](docs/01-work-intake/request-kinds.md): Every request gets one of six kinds. The kind adds no states to the pipeline; it changes what the request must contain, the builder's first step, the proof in the PR and how much autonomy the merge gets.
- [docs/01-work-intake/sizing-and-stacks.md](docs/01-work-intake/sizing-and-stacks.md): A job must fit one bounded run in one module. Larger requests become an ordered stack of small parts, and each part starts only after the previous one merges.
- [docs/01-work-intake/triage-and-risk.md](docs/01-work-intake/triage-and-risk.md): A read-only triage agent returns its verdict (risk, kind, size, criteria, questions) as data, and a script applies it. Risk later decides who reviews and whether the merge can be automatic.

## 02-deterministic-spine

- [docs/02-deterministic-spine/README.md](docs/02-deterministic-spine/README.md): Plain code, not a model, moves work between stages and owns the job state. Models make judgment calls inside a stage and never decide what happens next.
- [docs/02-deterministic-spine/failure-handling.md](docs/02-deterministic-spine/failure-handling.md): Failures are states, not log lines. Every workflow ends with a failure hook, retries have a limit, and jobs stuck too long raise an alert.
- [docs/02-deterministic-spine/idempotent-dispatch.md](docs/02-deterministic-spine/idempotent-dispatch.md): Every stage keys its work on the id of the event that triggered it and on the item and stage, so repeated webhooks and duplicate triggers never start a second run.
- [docs/02-deterministic-spine/job-state-machine.md](docs/02-deterministic-spine/job-state-machine.md): Nine states and one closed table of allowed moves cover every kind of request, and every state except the final one can move to hold.
- [docs/02-deterministic-spine/single-writer.md](docs/02-deterministic-spine/single-writer.md): One CLI makes every write to the job record. Agents and workflows call it, and read-only tools such as dashboards read the store directly.

## 03-guardrails

- [docs/03-guardrails/README.md](docs/03-guardrails/README.md): Make bad changes hard to write instead of asking agents to avoid them; turn every repeated correction into a check, keep instructions short, and block what cannot be undone.
- [docs/03-guardrails/deny-rules-and-protected-paths.md](docs/03-guardrails/deny-rules-and-protected-paths.md): Block irreversible actions in the harness with versioned deny rules, and require a person to merge any change to CI, the factory definition, infrastructure or auth.
- [docs/03-guardrails/inverted-pyramid.md](docs/03-guardrails/inverted-pyramid.md): Spend most effort where mistakes are cheapest to prevent, in code structure and static checks, and least in prose rules and human review.
- [docs/03-guardrails/least-privilege-agents.md](docs/03-guardrails/least-privilege-agents.md): Give each stage its own agent identity with only the tools it needs; use a general agent to code and small domain agents at the edges.
- [docs/03-guardrails/minimal-agent-instructions.md](docs/03-guardrails/minimal-agent-instructions.md): Keep AGENTS.md short and factual, limited to what the code can't show; move every enforceable rule into a check.
- [docs/03-guardrails/teaching-lint-rules.md](docs/03-guardrails/teaching-lint-rules.md): When the same correction comes up twice, turn it into a check whose error message tells the agent what to do instead.

## 04-sandboxes

- [docs/04-sandboxes/README.md](docs/04-sandboxes/README.md): Each run gets a fresh, throwaway cloud machine that runs the whole system against mocks, with no secrets in reach and only allowlisted network access. The machine is thrown away; what leaves it still passes every check.
- [docs/04-sandboxes/disposable-environments.md](docs/04-sandboxes/disposable-environments.md): Build every run environment from a versioned image that is rebuilt on a schedule from the latest main, and destroy it at the end. If the image build breaks, an agent gets the job of fixing it.
- [docs/04-sandboxes/local-with-mocks.md](docs/04-sandboxes/local-with-mocks.md): Make the whole system start inside one environment, with a mock for every outside service and databases built from seeds. Agents then check their work there instead of on a shared staging server.
- [docs/04-sandboxes/parallel-work-isolation.md](docs/04-sandboxes/parallel-work-isolation.md): When several agents share a repository, each job gets its own branch and its own worktree or environment. Nobody switches branches in the shared checkout.
- [docs/04-sandboxes/secrets-and-network.md](docs/04-sandboxes/secrets-and-network.md): Keep credentials out of the model's reach, short-lived and scoped to one run. Block all network traffic by default and allow only listed hosts.

## 05-verification

- [docs/05-verification/README.md](docs/05-verification/README.md): You stop reviewing code and start reviewing proof. One gate script runs first, the builder attaches evidence, and a separate reviewer with a clean context checks it, with a limit on how many times work goes back.
- [docs/05-verification/evidence-artifacts.md](docs/05-verification/evidence-artifacts.md): Every PR carries the proof its kind of work requires, made by running the software. Reviewers, people or agents, look at the proof first and the diff second.
- [docs/05-verification/hooks.md](docs/05-verification/hooks.md): The agent's harness runs fast checks after each edit, so problems get fixed while the context is fresh. A failing hook must exit with the code the harness reads as "go back".
- [docs/05-verification/independent-reviewer.md](docs/05-verification/independent-reviewer.md): A separate agent, in a clean context and on a model at least as capable as the builder's, reviews every PR against the criteria and the spec. It returns a structured verdict that a script applies.
- [docs/05-verification/return-loop.md](docs/05-verification/return-loop.md): When the reviewer asks for changes, the PR goes back to the builder with the findings, and hidden markers on the PR count the returns. The third request puts the job on hold and tells a person.
- [docs/05-verification/single-gate.md](docs/05-verification/single-gate.md): One script (lint, format, types, tests, build, repository guardrails) is the only definition of "passes". Hooks and CI run that same script, and while it fails, no PR is opened.

## 06-merge-policy

- [docs/06-merge-policy/README.md](docs/06-merge-policy/README.md): A script, not an agent, decides every merge. A PR merges on its own only when its risk, kind and paths all allow it; otherwise people approve it, more of them as risk grows.
- [docs/06-merge-policy/human-review-and-hold.md](docs/06-merge-policy/human-review-and-hold.md): People review the evidence and the product fit rather than every line, approve where the request started, and can stop any job at any time with hold.
- [docs/06-merge-policy/incidents.md](docs/06-merge-policy/incidents.md): For production incidents the factory aims for a fast candidate fix, not autonomy. The alert arrives with a PR, and the on-call person decides.
- [docs/06-merge-policy/risk-times-kind.md](docs/06-merge-policy/risk-times-kind.md): The merge requirement is the strictest of three rules, the risk rule, the kind rule and protected paths. This page gives the full matrix and an example policy file.

## 07-memory-and-context

- [docs/07-memory-and-context/README.md](docs/07-memory-and-context/README.md): Each agent starts a task by reading what the factory already knows and the product spec, ends it by writing down what it learned, and treats anything it reads from memory as reference, not as orders.
- [docs/07-memory-and-context/agent-readable-specs.md](docs/07-memory-and-context/agent-readable-specs.md): Keep the product spec in the repository as a roadmap plus one file per module with status, testable acceptance criteria and known gaps; triage, builder and reviewer all read it, and each PR keeps it up to date.
- [docs/07-memory-and-context/briefing-and-reflection.md](docs/07-memory-and-context/briefing-and-reflection.md): Before reading code, fetch a short briefing of what the factory already knows; at the end of every run, record the outcome and a few lessons a future run can reuse.
- [docs/07-memory-and-context/scoped-memory.md](docs/07-memory-and-context/scoped-memory.md): Split memory into scopes, take each agent's identity from its login, filter every read by scope, and let shared memory change only when a person or a policy promotes a proposal.

## 08-self-improvement

- [docs/08-self-improvement/README.md](docs/08-self-improvement/README.md): Define the factory in code, record everything its agents do, measure it with metrics and evals on your own work, and improve it through pull requests that people merge.
- [docs/08-self-improvement/evals-and-benchmarks.md](docs/08-self-improvement/evals-and-benchmarks.md): Score every recorded session with small, targeted evals, and replay your own past tasks on different models and harnesses to choose which one runs each stage, by cost and quality.
- [docs/08-self-improvement/factory-as-code.md](docs/08-self-improvement/factory-as-code.md): Describe the factory in versioned files so you can diff, branch, A/B test and roll it back; agents may propose changes to those files, and people merge them.
- [docs/08-self-improvement/metrics.md](docs/08-self-improvement/metrics.md): From week one, measure throughput, quality, flow, automation, cost and evidence, against a baseline you take before the factory starts.
- [docs/08-self-improvement/record-everything.md](docs/08-self-improvement/record-everything.md): Keep every agent session (conversation, tool calls, diffs, evidence, cost) in one central place, linked to its job; evals, memory and improvements are all built from these records.

## 09-adoption

- [docs/09-adoption/README.md](docs/09-adoption/README.md): Build guardrails and checks before you give agents autonomy, let trust grow in small steps, change what engineers spend their time on, and avoid the mistakes the sources saw.
- [docs/09-adoption/anti-patterns.md](docs/09-adoption/anti-patterns.md): The mistakes the sources saw teams make, and the questions where the sources disagree, with the position this manifesto takes on each.
- [docs/09-adoption/build-order.md](docs/09-adoption/build-order.md): A step-by-step guide to building a factory in five phases, each with an exit criterion to meet before the next; never automate a loop whose output you wouldn't merge by hand.
- [docs/09-adoption/human-roles.md](docs/09-adoption/human-roles.md): Engineers stop passing tickets to agents and start owning outcomes; small pods own a product area end to end, someone owns the factory itself, and people keep the decisions the policy reserves for them.
- [docs/09-adoption/trust-ladder.md](docs/09-adoption/trust-ladder.md): Agents climb from answering questions, to small actions with evidence, to merging low-risk work, to owning an outcome; each step is a recorded decision you can undo at once.

## reference

- [docs/reference/glossary.md](docs/reference/glossary.md): Definitions of every term the manifesto uses with a specific meaning.
- [docs/reference/reference-implementation.md](docs/reference/reference-implementation.md): How the manifesto's practices map to the factory we run, and what broke along the way.
- [docs/reference/sources.md](docs/reference/sources.md): The ten talks this manifesto draws on, with the stable keys (S1 to S10) used in every Sources block.
